$comment: Phase UI-17 reviewed frontend budget (UI/UX plan §6.5, §22.1, §22.4). Enforced by scripts/ui17-bundle-budget.mjs in CI. Caps were FROZEN from the pre-optimisation baseline (main 1e8bd5f7, 2026-10-13) before any UI-17 change was measured, never tuned to a post-change result. Raising a cap is a reviewed change with evidence; see docs/frontend/audits/ui-17/performance-baseline-and-budget.json.

method.measured_on: emitted bytes in public/spa (vite build); gzip level 6 = the edge's gzip_comp_level, i.e. the bytes nginx actually sends
method.initial_request: the entry chunk plus its static-import closure and CSS — what the Laravel shell names
method.critical_path: initial request plus the static closure of the archetype's route modules (layout + home page) — what a cold visit must fetch before the page can render

rationale.initial_request_js: Baseline 79,977 B. Cap 102,400 B (100 KiB) = +28% headroom: room for ordinary growth, but a single eagerly imported page, chart or editor library breaks it.
rationale.critical_path_js: Cap 170,000 B — the widely used mobile critical-path JS reference (~170 KB compressed for a usable first load on a mid-range phone over 4G). Baseline worst case is the Audit shell at 148,367 B (13% headroom); every archetype must stay under it.
rationale.critical_path_css: Baseline worst case 24,353 B (Audit shell). Cap 30,720 B.
rationale.critical_path_requests: Baseline worst case 64 (Audit shell). Cap 80: catches a module-graph explosion, leaves room for one more shared component split.
rationale.lazy_route_chunk: Largest route chunk at baseline 9,247 B (public landing). Cap 24,576 B (24 KiB): a page that grows 2.6x, or two pages merged into one chunk, is a review event.
rationale.lazy_content_chunk: Generated legal/FAQ/landing content is verbatim text (never paraphrased, UI/UX plan §17.2). Largest at baseline 54,163 B (HR Data Policy). Cap 65,536 B.

runtime_targets.$comment: Lab targets measured by scripts/ui17-web-vitals.mjs on the BUILT image origin. Lab p75 is nearest-rank over N lab samples, never field p75.
